day4_lunch_start.text: *The lunch bell rings. As the classroom door opens, the hallway fills with the sound of footsteps.*

day4_lunch_choice.text: *Lunch is the only window I have. I need to move fast.*
choices: Search for Yuna
Investigate the nurse's office
Go to the rooftop

day4_lunch_yuna_1.text: *The photography club room. The door is locked. It was open until yesterday.*

day4_lunch_yuna_2.text: *I looked around. Nobody in the hallway. One of the windows isn't fully locked. I squeezed through.*

day4_lunch_yuna_3.text: *Yuna's locker. Empty. Even the dust on the floor has been wiped away in a neat square.*

day4_lunch_yuna_4.text: *The other lockers are dusty. Only Yuna's is clean, with wet cloth strokes left in an inside corner.*

day4_lunch_yuna_5.text: *The plywood at the bottom of the locker is slightly raised. A false bottom. Yuna's camera is hidden inside.*

day4_lunch_yuna_6.text: *I took the camera out. Almost no battery left. I powered it on.*

day4_lunch_yuna_7.text: *The photo list contains over 200 images, mostly of the school. Suited figures keep appearing in the corners. Their faces differ, but they stand in the same spots.*

day4_lunch_yuna_8.text: *The last photo: stairs leading underground. In the corner, handwritten text: **'Down here -- Yu'***

day4_lunch_yuna_9.text: *The file info says it was taken last night at 22:41. Under that, battery remaining: 7%.*

day4_lunch_yuna_10.text: *End of the old building hallway. 'Authorized Personnel Only.' A rusted door.*

day4_lunch_yuna_11.text: *I pulled the handle. It won't open. A new padlock on a rusted door. Paint dust around the latch is still scattered on the threshold.*

day4_lunch_yuna_12.text: *I pressed my ear to the gap in the door. I can hear something below. A low mechanical hum. And — a short sound, like someone swallowing their breath. Once. Then once again.*

day4_lunch_yuna_14.text: *I rattled the padlock. It won't budge. I searched my pockets. Nothing that could open it.*

day4_lunch_yuna_15.text: *Footsteps. From the end of the hallway. Someone is coming.*

day4_lunch_yuna_16.text: *I drew my heels tight into the shadow. The click of shoes stopped on the flakes of paint along the basement threshold.*

day4_lunch_yuna_17.text: *Ms. Eunsu walked to the end of the corridor and unlocked the padlock with a key. Once she stepped inside and shut the door, a bolt slid into place from the inside.*

day4_lunch_yuna_18.text: *The metallic click of the turning key still lingers in my ears. Beyond the closed door, the low mechanical hum continues.*
choices: Look for the key tonight
Retrace Ms. Riin's movements
Follow the clue Seolhwa left

day4_lunch_yuna_19.text: *I clenched my fist. My nails dig into my palm.*

day4_lunch_yuna_20.text: *I have to open this door tomorrow.*

day4_lunch_nurse_1.text: *Ms. Riin is standing before the medicine cabinet, drawing a clear liquid into a syringe.*

day4_lunch_nurse_first.text:
*The nameplate on the desk catches my eye first: 'Kang Riin, school nurse.' As I read it, someone in a white coat looks up from inside.*

Ma'am, can we talk for a moment?

day4_lunch_nurse_2.text: *I can see the label on the ampoule. 'M-13'. The font is different from the cold medicine label in the next slot.*

day4_lunch_nurse_3.text:
*Her fingertips pause as she picks up the syringe from the tray the moment her eyes meet mine.*

What was that just now?

day4_lunch_nurse_5.text:
*She quietly slips the syringe behind her back. Before the hem of her white coat hides it, the clear graduation marks catch my eye.*

I saw all of it. Hiding it now won't let me pretend I didn't.

day4_lunch_nurse_noyuna.text: What were you doing just now?

day4_lunch_nurse_noyuna_2.text: ...A vitamin shot. You missed the group checkup today.

day4_lunch_nurse_noyuna_3.text:
*Even while hiding the syringe, Riin's fingers are covering the measuring lines. The ampoule label `M-13` is half visible behind the back of her hand.*

If it's vitamins, why cover the markings? Move your hand.

day4_lunch_nurse_6.text: They say Yuna suddenly transferred out. Did you know about that too?

day4_lunch_nurse_7.text:
A transfer means somewhere to go. Do you know where Yuna went?

*Nurse Riin presses the syringe cap down once more. Click. Only then does she answer.*

day4_lunch_nurse_8.text: ...Why are you staring like that? {name}, where did you go during lunch today?

day4_lunch_nurse_9.text:
*Her voice went cold for an instant, then turned gentle again.*

Not my lunch. We're talking about Yuna.

day4_lunch_nurse_11.text:
*After finishing her answer, Ms. Riin picks up the cup and carries it over to the sink tap.*

Saying she'll be fine—does that mean she isn't right now?

day4_lunch_nurse_12.text:
*She turns the tap all the way on to rinse the cup, the rushing water filling the silence between answers.*

Let's check your face first. We can talk in a bit.

day4_lunch_nurse_13.text: ...You look tired. Like you haven't slept.

day4_lunch_nurse_14.text: Do you want something that will help?

day4_lunch_nurse_15.text:
*She smiles as she speaks, yet one hand still holds the syringe.*

Hold on. Put that syringe down first before we talk.
choices: Refuse right away
Ask the name of the drug
Bring up Yuna

day4_lunch_nurse_16.text: *I refuse and leave. Behind me, Nurse Riin mutters under her breath.*

day4_lunch_roof_1.text: *Words carved beneath the railing. Deep gouges made with a knife.*

day4_lunch_roof_2.text: *I bend down for a closer look. The writing is old, but unmistakable.*

day4_lunch_roof_3.text: ***'There's only one way out. -- Lee Seolhwa'***

day4_lunch_roof_4.text: *Small text below: **'The answer is in the basement'***
choices: Memorize the words
Photograph the message

day4_lunch_roof_5.text: *I touched the letters with my fingers. Cold. Writing carved into a metal railing. Old marks.*

day4_lunch_roof_6.text: *Rust powder clung to my fingertips. The inside of the carved letters is the color of something long washed by rainwater.*

day4_lunch_roof_7.text: *Lee Seolhwa. The final stroke of the name is carved deep into the inside of the railing.*

day4_lunch_nurse_ask_name_2.text: A supplement. You don't need the label. Just lie down.

day4_lunch_nurse_ask_yuna.text: Did you give Yuna that too?

day4_lunch_nurse_ask_yuna_2.text: Save talk about Yuna for tomorrow. Right now, let's take care of your medicine first.

day4_lunch_nurse_leave_ask.text: *I leave without waiting for more. Behind me an ampoule clicks against the tray.*

day4_lunch_nurse_leave_yuna.text: *After I brought up Yuna's name, I couldn't ask any more questions. As I stepped out into the hallway, a low sigh slipped through the crack in the door.*

day4_lunch_darkroom_1.text: A drop of water fell from inside the dark room. Two wet tongs were placed next to the printing tank.

day4_lunch_darkroom_2.text: Contact sheets were hanging over the net. Faces sitting at the same desk lined up in each small cubicle.

day4_lunch_darkroom_3.text: I counted the squares with my fingers and found that only the twelfth square had the edge of the water not yet dried.

day4_lunch_darkroom_4.text: When the red light was turned on, a face appeared in the film. The hair and uniform were different, but the shape of the left hand held was the same.

day4_lunch_darkroom_5.text: The twelfth person was not looking at the camera. He was handing something to someone outside the photo.

day4_lunch_darkroom_6.text: Yuna's fingers were slightly imprinted under the wrist. A pincer was covering that part.

day4_lunch_darkroom_7.text: As I moved the tongs, I saw small footprints on the glass. Yuna seemed to have made a hasty turn here.

day4_lunch_darkroom_8.text: Instead of taking photo paper with me, I took a picture of the entire thing with my phone and then took another picture of the part where my hands overlapped.

day4_lunch_darkroom_9.text: The wet bag seemed to change shape when touched.
choices: Even the position of the tongs is taken in a photo.
Look at the footprints on the door first.
Wait without touching the object

day4_lunch_darkroom_10.text: The end of the film inside the envelope was cut. I measured the remaining length and thought about where I would have moved it.

day4_lunch_darkroom_11.text: I switched off the red safelight and peered through the gap in the darkroom curtain toward the photography clubroom.

day4_lunch_darkroom_12.text: The hallway was still quiet. The screen of Yuna's camera, which I'd turned on earlier, glowed faintly in front of the lockers.

day4_lunch_yuna_hide_1.text: I checked the keyhole in front of the basement door. Beyond the crack, only a low mechanical hum and ragged breathing seeped out.

day4_lunch_yuna_hide_2.text: My shoe slipped once on the stairs. The flashlight beam came down from under the wall.

day4_lunch_yuna_hide_3.text: I opened the cleaning toolbox door and pushed the two brooms inside, leaving a gap for a body to fit in.

day4_lunch_yuna_hide_4.text: The moment I closed the door, the cell phone in my pocket hit the shelf. I wrapped my hand around it, but a short sound was already coming out.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_choice.text: The light from the crack in the door caught the back of my hand. The sound of footsteps stopped at the bottom of the stairs.
choices: Cover your phone with clothes and do not move it
Come out first and say you're lost

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_safe_1.text: The smell of work clothes reached my nose. I put my sleeve in my mouth and pressed the phone to my stomach.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_safe_2.text: You kept the door locked, right? I'm heading down now, so I'll check it myself.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_safe_3.text: A short beep ended the call. The flashlight beam skimming the crack of the door shifted toward the basement entrance.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_safe_4.text: The click of heels passed the janitor's closet and headed to the end of the corridor. Holding my breath, I squeezed the broom handle tight.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_safe_5.text: Through the narrow gap by the hinges, I caught a sliver of the rusted door at the end of the corridor.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_fail_1.text: The door handle moved first. The tip of Ms. Eunsu's shoe stopped right in front of the open gap.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_fail_2.text: If you got lost, you should've called a teacher. Students aren't supposed to come down here.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_fail_3.text: I lowered my head and pushed my phone deep into my pocket. The teacher held the door until my hand came out.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_fail_4.text: Head back up to your classroom and wait. Let's talk again after lunch.

day4_lunch_yuna_breath_fail_5.text: I pretended to step toward the stairs she pointed to, then flattened myself into the shadow around the corner and listened behind me.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_1.text: Three glass ampoules were placed on a metal tray. Only the area where the label was torn off remained translucent.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_2.text: When Ms. Riin pushed the drawer shut, the torn edge of a sheet of paper caught in the gap. Before her white coat blocked it, I glimpsed a small printed grid.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_3.text: Wash your hands and come back. You came in from outside.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_4.text: The teacher's hand was reflected in the sink mirror. She pushed one ampoule aside and lined up only the other two.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_5.text: The capped syringe still lay on the tray. Instead of picking it up, she washed the cup first.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_6.text: Have you had anything for breakfast? I'm not giving you medicine before food.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_7.text: As I turned off the faucet, I heard the sound of the health room clock. The teacher also looked in the same direction for a moment.

day4_lunch_nurse_tray_8.text: The piece of paper remained in the crevice of the drawer. Before turning around, I counted the number of grids with my eyes.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_1.text: You can't leave this place either, can you?

day4_lunch_nurse_key_2.text: Ms. Riin lowered the fingers resting on the rim of the cup. The glass touched the tray and chimed once.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_3.text: Don't say that in the hallway.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_4.text: When I tried to look at the camera beside the door, she stepped in front of me. Metal clinked briefly inside her coat pocket.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_5.text: A keyring caught on the edge of her pocket. She didn't push it back inside—just drew her hand away.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_6.text: Finding a lost thing doesn't mean you have to hand it back straight away.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_7.text: My eyes moved from my pocket to the door. The teacher moved out of the way to create a passage.

day4_lunch_nurse_key_8.text: I left the health room without touching the key and only remembering which pocket it was in.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_1.text: I asked when Yuna had last come by. Ms. Riin closed the logbook and tied its string.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_2.text: There's no departure time in her record. I didn't write one down.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_3.text: The end of the tied string slipped off the teacher's fingers. She started to tie it again, then left it as it was.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_4.text: If there's only a record of her coming in, officially she hasn't left. Remember that.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_5.text: When I glanced at the drawer, the teacher quietly shook her head and took a step toward the door.

day4_lunch_nurse_yuna_6.text: The lunchtime broadcast drifted outside the nurse's office. Before the door shut, I heard her washing one more cup.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_1.text: When I dusted off the exposed concrete under the wire mesh, several deep lines emerged.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_2.text: It was seven vertical strokes and an arrow pointing to the left. Rust had accumulated in the shallow scratches.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_3.text: I tried putting my fingernail into the line. There were several instances where my fingers slipped while trying to write.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_4.text: The sand had hardened inside the scratched line.
choices: Take pictures by changing the direction of light
Look under the wire mesh fixture
Read with your eyes, without using your hands

day4_lunch_roof_etch_5.text: When I opened my left hand, the lines in my palm folded in the same direction. Even when I took my hand away, sand remained at my fingertips.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_6.text: The wire mesh behind me rang lightly. When I turned around, Seolhwa was standing next to the staircase door.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_7.text: If you come this far, you can see outside. So everyone comes here first.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_8.text: Seolhwa didn't come near the railing; with her fingers, she was folding the cuff of a sleeve that wasn't even wet.

day4_lunch_roof_etch_9.text: I did the same. Seeing the buses beyond the fence made me think I could reach them.

day4_lunch_roof_memory_choice.text: Seolhwa looked toward the left stairwell. I let go of the wire mesh.
choices: Why didn't you head out toward the main gate?
What happened at the emergency exit back then?

day4_lunch_roof_fence_1.text: Look down. There's only one road beyond the fence. You'd be caught before a bus arrived.

day4_lunch_roof_fence_2.text: Looking down through the wire mesh, I saw a security office located between the school entrance and the bus stop.

day4_lunch_roof_fence_3.text: The doors you see by day aren't the ones that open at night. I learned that too late in the seventh cycle.

day4_lunch_roof_fence_4.text: Seolhwa's bangs moved in the wind. The other sleeve was folded against the wind direction.

day4_lunch_roof_fence_5.text: You can open the old building's emergency exit by hand. Locking it outside doesn't remove the inside handle.

day4_lunch_roof_exit_1.text: I opened it first. Your hands were full of documents.

day4_lunch_roof_exit_2.text: When I looked down at my left hand, Seolhwa also looked at the same side. I tried to straighten my fingers but clenched my fist.

day4_lunch_roof_exit_3.text: Someone came to the door. They knew we'd brought the papers.

day4_lunch_roof_exit_4.text: Seolhwa pretended to hold the door handle. The hand stopped in the air and tendons rose on the back of the hand.

day4_lunch_roof_exit_5.text: Details are in the records there. Don’t tell me you remember everything just by listening to me.

day4_lunch_roof_second_choice.text: The staircase door was slightly opened by the wind. Seolhwa retreated there first.
choices: This time I'll start by looking for records.
Ask again for the location of the left emergency exit.

day4_lunch_roof_record_1.text: Good. You don't have to pretend you remember just to agree with me. Read the papers yourself.

day4_lunch_roof_record_2.text: I took out my phone and took a picture of the scratch. Only the wire mesh and hands remained on the screen, and Seolhwa was not visible.

day4_lunch_roof_record_3.text: After saving the photo, I looked up again and heard the sound of the staircase door closing.

day4_lunch_roof_left_1.text: Left, in the basement. Don't count the stairs. Find the door with the handle that opens inward.

day4_lunch_roof_left_2.text: I dusted the sand from my palms onto the lining of my pockets and repeated the word left in my mouth once.

day4_lunch_roof_left_3.text: When I turned my head toward the stairs, the rooftop door stood half open. No human shadow stretched beyond the gap.

day4_history_callback_28.text: The photo I received on the first day was also lit in the same direction. Now I can see why Yuna told me not to fold the paper.

day4_history_callback_29.text: I measured the distance between the spot where I found the camera and this envelope. They were both hidden on the same side of the door.

day4_history_callback_30.text: The neck shape was the same as the ampoule seen earlier. Even if the label was removed, even small scratches on the glass were not removed.

day4_history_callback_31.text: Ms. Riin motioned for me to turn my phone face down. Just like when I tried shutting off the app on the first day, only the screen went dark while the location icon stayed lit.

day4_history_callback_32.text: I remembered Seolhwa's comment that when you hold the grip of a ballpoint pen, the folded area is pressed again and your hand orients itself first.

day4_history_callback_33.text: I touched the piece of paper in my pocket. I was still not sure if the jade, which was smudged and unreadable, was the rooftop.

day4_expansion_action_6_a.text: I framed the shot to catch the shadow of the print tongs as well—a marker to line up the exact spot when I need to find it again later.

day4_expansion_action_6_b.text: The wet spot on the front door was only on the inside side. I walked towards the wall without stepping on it.

day4_expansion_action_7_a.text: When I held my phone low, the shadow of the stroke became longer and I was able to distinguish between the smudges that looked like letters and the actual fine lines.

day4_expansion_action_7_b.text: The final stroke continued below the fastener. It seemed like traces of the old days remained beneath the newly erected wire mesh.
